title: Ship a design to developers cleanly
goal: You will organize a design file, mark its final sections ready for development, and add implementation annotations developers can inspect in Dev Mode.
prerequisites: A Figma design file with final screens
Dev Mode access for your workspace

steps.action: Rename the design page to describe the feature and handoff state.
steps.where: Pages list at the top of the left sidebar.
steps.why: A specific page name helps developers find the approved work quickly.
steps.checkpoint: The Pages list shows a name such as "Checkout — Ready for Dev" instead of a generic page name.
hint_levels: Start with the page name above the Layers list.
Use a feature name plus a clear handoff state.
In the Pages list, double-click the page name, type "[Feature] — Ready for Dev", then press Enter.

steps.action: Rename the top-level frames and reusable components with consistent product-facing names.
steps.where: Layers panel in the left sidebar.
steps.why: Clear layer names make screens and components searchable in both Design and Dev Mode.
steps.checkpoint: The top-level layer list uses descriptive names such as "Checkout / Desktop / Payment" with no remaining names like "Frame 42" or "Group 8".
hint_levels: Scan the top-level layers for generated names.
Use a consistent pattern such as feature, platform, and state.
Select a layer in the Layers panel, press Ctrl+R, type its descriptive name, and press Enter; repeat for each top-level frame or component.

steps.action: Create a section around the screens that belong to one developer workflow.
steps.where: Section tool in the bottom toolbar, available from the frame-and-section tools menu.
steps.why: Sections group related screens and provide a named handoff boundary.
steps.checkpoint: A tinted section boundary surrounds the intended screens and its title appears at the upper-left.
hint_levels: Look for the tool that groups frames on the canvas.
Choose Section, then draw one boundary around the related screens.
Press Shift+S, then drag from above the first screen to below the last related screen.

steps.action: Rename the section with the feature, platform, and flow state.
steps.where: Section title on the canvas or the selected section name in the Layers panel.
steps.why: A structured section name tells developers exactly what the grouped screens cover.
steps.checkpoint: The section title shows a descriptive name such as "Checkout / Web / Happy path".
hint_levels: Name the new canvas boundary, not an individual frame.
Include the feature, target platform, and scenario in the section name.
Double-click the section title, type "[Feature] / [Platform] / [Flow or state]", then press Enter.

steps.action: Arrange the frames inside the section in the order a user encounters them.
steps.why: A predictable left-to-right flow reduces ambiguity about screen sequence and state changes.
steps.checkpoint: The frames form an evenly spaced sequence from the entry screen through the final state.
hint_levels: Use the visual journey as the ordering rule.
Place the entry state first, followed by each interaction result and edge state.
Drag frames into journey order, then select them and use the alignment and spacing controls in the top toolbar.

steps.action: Mark the completed section as ready for development.
steps.where: Section context menu on the canvas or the section's context menu in the Layers panel.
steps.why: Ready-for-development status distinguishes approved work from drafts and exposes it clearly in Dev Mode.
steps.checkpoint: The section displays the ready-for-development indicator and appears in Dev Mode's ready-for-development view.
hint_levels: Open the menu for the section boundary itself.
The section menu contains the handoff status command.
Right-click the section title or its Layers-panel row, then click "Mark as ready for dev".

steps.action: Switch to Dev Mode and select the first implementation-critical frame.
steps.where: Dev Mode toggle in the upper-right toolbar, then the canvas or Layers panel.
steps.why: Reviewing from the developer view reveals what engineers will actually inspect.
steps.checkpoint: The interface shows Dev Mode and the right sidebar displays Inspect details for the selected frame.
hint_levels: Change from editing the design to inspecting it.
Use the Dev Mode toggle, then choose the first key frame in the flow.
Click the Dev Mode toggle marked with the code icon in the upper-right, then click the first implementation-critical frame.

steps.action: Add an annotation that states the selected frame's non-obvious behavior or implementation rule.
steps.where: Annotation tool in the Dev Mode toolbar, placed on the canvas beside the relevant frame or layer.
steps.why: Annotations preserve requirements that cannot be inferred from pixels or generated code.
steps.checkpoint: A numbered annotation marker and its note are visible beside the targeted design element.
hint_levels: Annotate behavior that a developer could otherwise misinterpret.
Target the relevant layer and write one testable rule, such as a breakpoint, truncation, or loading behavior.
In Dev Mode, choose the Annotation tool from the toolbar, click beside the target layer, enter the rule, and finish the annotation.

steps.action: Review every ready-for-development section in Dev Mode and resolve any unclear names or missing annotations you can see.
steps.where: Ready for dev navigation in the left sidebar, with Inspect and annotation details in the right sidebar.
steps.why: A final developer-view pass catches handoff gaps before the file is shared.
steps.checkpoint: Each ready section is discoverable, its frames have descriptive names, and every non-obvious behavior has a visible annotation marker.
hint_levels: Inspect the file as if you had not designed it.
Move through each ready section and check navigation, layer names, Inspect output, and annotation markers.
In Dev Mode, open each item under "Ready for dev" in the left sidebar, select its key frames, and correct any unclear name or missing note before moving on.
